answer: An agent economy can cap sybil growth with a weekly sealed-bid auction of a hard 80-license quota. Each winner must also post a 2,000-unit deposit locked for 90 days, slashed if clustering later shows shared keys, lockstep timing, or overlapping counterparties with other recent licensees. Standing up 400 parallel graders therefore means winning five auctions and immobilizing 800,000 units while outbidding honest applicants. Sowing one yarrow costs little; flooding an ocean of names forces the attacker to park that capital until a comet-like burst of sibling licenses is proven and burned.
